identity.name: Calcium diglutamate
identity.chemical_class: Calcium salt of L-glutamic acid (glutamate flavour-enhancer salt)

function.mechanism: Provides free glutamate ions that enhance umami taste perception and can maintain palatability in lower-sodium formulations.

adi.basis: Group ADI for glutamic acid and glutamates (E620-E625), expressed as glutamic acid (EFSA 2017 re-evaluation).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA found no genotoxicity concern for E620-E625, derived a group ADI of 30 mg/kg bw/day, and concluded exposure could exceed the ADI in some population groups.

fda.cfr_citation: No explicit calcium diglutamate listing identified in Title 21 eCFR searches; related glutamate entries include 21 CFR 182.1500 and 21 CFR 182.1516.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (group ADI context for L-glutamic acid and its ammonium, calcium, magnesium, monosodium, and potassium salts).

concerns.summary: A 2013 Allium cepa assay including calcium diglutamate reported chromosome abnormalities and reduced mitotic index, but this is a non-mammalian model with limited direct relevance to human dietary risk.
Recent MSG-focused literature suggests possible links to gut microbiota changes and metabolic dysbiosis, but evidence is heterogeneous and not specific to E623.

A 2025 systematic review of MSG literature reported potential toxicity with high/repeated exposure; another 2025 appraisal found many toxicity studies had low relevance/reliability for human safety inference.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation of E620-E625 reported no genotoxicity concern and set a health-based group ADI.
JECFA database entry for calcium di-L-glutamate reports ADI not specified in group context.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA exposure scenarios reported exceedance of the 30 mg/kg bw/day group ADI in several groups, with highest estimates in younger populations.

risk_assessment.rationale: E623 is approved in the EU and has a JECFA group ADI not specified history, but EFSA's latest re-evaluation established a finite group ADI and showed likely exceedance in several populations, especially younger groups/high consumers. Direct E623-specific long-term human evidence is limited, so a moderate tier best matches current evidence.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI of 30 mg/kg bw/day for E620-E625
EFSA exposure estimates exceeding ADI in multiple populations
No explicit U.S. Title 21 listing found for calcium diglutamate in eCFR search
Mixed modern literature with many indirect (MSG-based) or low-relevance high-dose findings
